solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What's written after fantastic pit stops with little credit added

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters of the two words are rearranged freely

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit in accounts

explanation.surface: A motor-racing scene: some remarkable pit stops, with a small credit tacked on at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges PIT STOPS together with the added CR.
explanation.definitionFit: A PS is a note added after the signature of a letter, so it is something written afterwards.

clue.text: Vanity shown by narrow-minded politician

parts.note: PO is short for po-faced, prim and humourless, here taken as narrow-minded
MP, Member of Parliament, is the stock politician

explanation.surface: A politician with a closed mind putting on a show of self-importance.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is a colloquial clipping of 'po-faced', a British term for prim and disapproving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ostentatious display, a kind of vain show of grandeur.

clue.text: Relocate to Tunisia for employment

indicators.note: to relocate is to move somewhere else, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to move to North Africa for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relocate' rearranges the letters of TO TUNISIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a job or post, as in 'situations vacant', so it means employment.

clue.text: Small wine jar

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A little container of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a vessel for the wine but is the verb or noun meaning a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a sudden jolt or unpleasant surprise, which is what a jolt to the system is.

clue.text: Do up residence with rent

parts.note: RES is the standard short form of residence, as in estate agents' 'des res'
rent is the past tense of rend, to tear, so it means tore

explanation.surface: Renovating a house while paying the rent on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment for the residence but is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up an old building is to renovate it, bringing it back to its former condition.

clue.text: Feature of shirt left in wrapper

indicators.note: in tells us one letter is placed inside the wrapper word

parts.note: a packet is a paper or card wrapper for goods

explanation.surface: A shirt still in its shop packaging, with some feature left showing.
explanation.definitionFit: A placket is the slit opening at a shirt's neck or cuff where the buttons fasten.

clue.text: Plough-jogger capriciously holds back a good day's work?

indicators.note: back means the held letters are to be read from right to left
the words hold the answer within them, spanning the join of two words

explanation.surface: A whimsical ploughman holding back from what should be a full day's ploughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds back' finds ERCA inside 'jogger capriciously' and reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre was traditionally the area of land one man with an ox team could plough in a day.

clue.text: Cold oik garners influence

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
an oik is a British word for a boorish, uncouth person, a lout

explanation.surface: A boorish lad with a cold manages to gain some sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garners' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is informal for power or sway, as in 'political clout'.

clue.text: Begin quietly then grow readiness for undertaking

parts.note: to enter on something is to begin it, as in entering a new phase
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to rise is to grow or increase

explanation.surface: Starting softly and then building up, ready for a new venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise is initiative, a willingness to take on new and bold projects.

clue.text: Tossing caber, so I will find a way to keep fit?

indicators.note: tossing throws things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Highland games athlete reckons caber tossing will keep them in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing' belongs to the caber in the surface but rearranges CABER SO I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobics is a programme of rhythmic exercise done to improve fitness.

clue.text: New term for dispensing with borders in transport system

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of this word are reshaped
dispensing with borders strips the outer letters off the next word, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A fresh name adopted for a transport network, dropping its boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TERM to METR; 'for' minus its outer letters leaves O.
explanation.definitionFit: A metro is an underground railway system serving a city, such as the Paris Métro.

clue.text: Southern headland attack — one's sure to get blamed

parts.note: a cape is a headland jutting into the sea
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: An attack on a southern headland, and someone is certain to carry the can for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is a person made to bear the blame for others' faults.

clue.text: Cope with assignment being penny-a-line stuff

parts.note: to hack something is informal for coping with it, as in 'can't hack it'
an assignment is a piece of work set

explanation.surface: Handling a task that pays only a pittance per line.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackwork is dull writing done for pay; penny-a-line describes poorly paid jobbing journalism.

clue.text: Page on this mammal would make you a children's writer

indicators.note: this says the page letter set on the answer produces the writer, so taking it away from the writer leaves the answer

parts.note: Beatrix Potter wrote children's books such as Peter Rabbit

explanation.surface: A bookish idea: a page about this animal turns you into a writer for children.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: P placed before the answer gives Beatrix Potter, so remove the P from her surname. 'on' sets the page in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating aquatic mammal of rivers and coasts.

clue.text: Talk whimsy about superior drink?

indicators.note: about here means turned around and moved, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Speaking fanciful nonsense over a fine drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TALK WHIMSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt whisky, especially single malt, is regarded as a premium spirit, finer than blended.

clue.text: Jenny's often like this — Anne is possibly embracing one

indicators.note: embracing means the scrambled letters wrap around another
possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters is in play

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remark about a woman called Jenny and her friend Anne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a woman's name but is a female donkey. 'possibly' rearranges ANNE IS around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A jenny is a she-ass, and anything like an ass is stupid, which is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Independent daughter being in character

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
an entity is a being, something that exists

explanation.surface: A self-reliant daughter showing her true personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' looks like a phrase but 'being' is a noun and 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's identity is one's individual character, what makes a person who they are.

clue.text: Balding husband disappearing into a state of invisibility?

indicators.note: disappearing tells us a letter vanishes from the phrase

parts.note: someone balding has thin hair
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man losing his hair until he vanishes altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish into thin air is to disappear without trace, so it is a fanciful place where things cannot be seen.

clue.text: Trailer on truck with electronic ID first to benefit

indicators.note: first places the identification ahead of the electronic letter in the build

parts.note: a trailer is an advertisement for a film, so an ad
a van is a goods-carrying truck
a tag is an identifying label
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in email

explanation.surface: A vehicle trailer and an electronic tag, both helpful to the haulier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' is a film preview, not a towed vehicle. 'first' puts TAG before E rather than the e-tag order.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a benefit or favourable circumstance.

clue.text: Nearly all of team drink around Spain and become tight

parts.note: a football or cricket team has eleven players, so nearly all of one is ten

indicators.note: around means the drink word goes round the country letter

parts.note: to sup is to drink
E is Spain's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Most of a team drinking in Spain and getting tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' suggests drunkenness in the surface, but here means taut.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense up is to become stiff and taut, through nerves or effort.

clue.text: Not quite the most unhealthy-looking snacks

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: pastiest means palest and most sickly-looking

explanation.surface: Snacks that look almost as unhealthy as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasties are pastry turnovers with a savoury filling, eaten as snacks; a Cornish pasty is the classic.

clue.text: With regard to two travel documents, the last is incomplete

indicators.note: the second of the pair loses its final letter
two asks for the travel document word to be written twice

parts.note: a visa is an entry permit stamped in a passport

explanation.surface: Paperwork for a trip, one document not filled in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, borrowed from French, means in relation to or compared with.

clue.text: Vigor (sic) in volume in vogue upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a rage is a craze or vogue, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: An editor's note flagging an American spelling, with books and fashion in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: '(sic)' flags the American spelling of vigour; this sense of the answer, energy, is mainly American, as in 'piss and vinegar'.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang vinegar means vim or energetic spirit.

clue.text: Surprising success surrounding sailor's customary dress

indicators.note: surrounding means the success word goes around the sailor

parts.note: a hit is a success, often an unexpected smash
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's surprising triumph, dressed in the usual uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is the usual garment of a monk or nun, or a riding habit, a customary costume.

clue.text: Reason I'll get stuck into health food

indicators.note: get stuck into means the single letter is pushed inside the food word

parts.note: bran is the husk of grain, eaten as a fibre-rich health food

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to tuck into some healthy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get stuck into' reads as eating heartily but places I inside BRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain stands for intellect or reasoning power, as in 'use your brain'.

clue.text: Succeeded along with count in bar

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
and joins things, meaning along with
to count on someone is to bank on them

explanation.surface: Success and a nobleman, apparently in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman but means rely, and 'bar' is not a pub but a ridge of sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbank is a ridge of sand in the sea or a river, also called a sandbar.

clue.text: Company in grip of embargo is what one often wants to save

definitions.text: what one often wants to save

indicators.note: in grip of means the company letters are held inside the ban

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: A firm caught by a trade embargo, desperate to rescue something.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'save one's bacon' means escape trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To save one's bacon is to escape harm, so it is the thing people often wish to rescue.

clue.text: Bath time barney

parts.note: Bath is a famous English spa town, so a spa

explanation.surface: A quarrel during bath time.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city famous for its Roman baths. 'barney' is British slang for a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, the same as a row or squabble.

clue.text: Shy holding acid, causing alarm

indicators.note: holding means the throwing word contains the sour one

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy, so to sling
tart means sharp or acid in taste

explanation.surface: A timid person carrying acid is a worrying sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling gives a sudden fright or surprise, so it causes alarm.

clue.text: Incline to follow Conservative stiffness

indicators.note: to follow means the slope word comes after the party letter

parts.note: a ramp is an inclined slope

explanation.surface: A Tory suffering stiffness from going up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramp is a painful involuntary tightening of a muscle, a seizing stiffness.

clue.text: Jerk, Virginia's son?

definitions.meaning: a native son of Virginia is an American, colloquially called by the short form of Yankee

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that Virginians, being Southerners, would hardly call themselves Yankees.
explanation.definitionFit: A yank is a sharp tug, and Yank is slang for any American.

clue.text: A rigorous preparation for toning the skin

parts.note: stringent means strict and rigorous

explanation.surface: A demanding beauty regime.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent is a lotion that tightens the pores and tones the skin.
